subject: Biology
source: IISER IAT 2025, final answer key (English), iiseradmission.in
_transcription: Biology = pages p01-p16, printed numbers 1-15, one question per page from p01 to p13 and p15-p16; p14 is the continuation of Q13 (its options (c) and (d)) with no question number. Numbers checked unbroken 1..15 against the 'N. Question N' headings. Q11's cross diagram is plain text (parents, F1, gamete percentages) and is typed, not cropped. Q13 has a gel picture (stem figure) and four plasmid-map pictures as options (a, b on p13; c, d on p14).

rows.text:
Match the entries in column I and column II.

| | Column I | | Column II |
|---|---|---|---|
| P. | Notochord and hollow nerve cord present | i. | Cyclostomata |
| Q. | Ectoparasite with 6-15 pairs of gills and closed circulation | ii. | Chondrichthyes |
| R. | Marine animals with persistent notochord and placoid scales | iii. | Hemichordata |
| S. | Animals with open circulatory systems, and stomochord | iv. | Chordata |

Which one of the following combinations is correct?
options: P - iv; Q - i; R - ii; S - iii
P - iv; Q - ii; R - i; S - iii
P - i; Q - iii; R - ii; S - iv
P - iii; Q - i; R - ii; S - iv

rows.text: Chromosomes are classified as metacentric, sub-metacentric, acrocentric and telocentric. This classification is based on the position of which one of the following structures?
options: Centromere
Centrosome
Centriole
Telomere

rows.text: Which one of the following options describes a triglyceride?
options: Three fatty acid chains linked to a molecule of glycerol
Three glycerol molecules linked to a fatty acid chain
Three saturated fatty acid chains linked to a molecule of cholesterol
Three glyceride molecules linked to a molecule of phospholipid

rows.text: Which one of the following statements about a plant carotenoid is FALSE?
options: It is an accessory pigment which absorbs light at 600 - 700 nm.
It protects chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.
It provides precursor for the synthesis of stress hormone in plants.
It accumulates in chromoplasts during fruit ripening.

rows.text:
A cell suspension of actively respiring mitochondria is treated with either chemical X (experiment 1) or chemical Y (experiment 2), or left untreated (experiment 3).

Chemical X selectively inhibits electron transport from Complex I to ubiquinone, while chemical Y selectively inhibits electron transport from Complex III to cytochrome C.

Which one of the following options represents the correct order of relative number of ATP synthesised in mitochondria?
options: Experiment 2 \(<\) Experiment 1 \(<\) Experiment 3
Experiment 1 \(<\) Experiment 2 \(<\) Experiment 3
Experiment 1 \(=\) Experiment 2 \(=\) Experiment 3
Experiment 2 \(<\) Experiment 1 \(=\) Experiment 3

rows.text: Which one of the following autoregulatory mechanisms is employed by the kidney when glomerular filtration rate is reduced?
options: Levels of renin, angiotensin I and II and aldosterone are increased.
Levels of renin and aldosterone are reduced.
Levels of renin are increased, while those of angiotensin I and II and aldosterone are reduced.
Levels of angiotensin I and II are increased, while that of aldosterone are reduced.

rows.text: Which one of the following conditions will favour maximum dissociation of oxygen from the oxyhaemoglobin in the tissues?
options: higher \(\mathrm{[H^+]}\); higher temperature
higher \(\mathrm{[H^+]}\); lower temperature
lower \(\mathrm{[H^+]}\); higher temperature
lower \(\mathrm{[H^+]}\); lower temperature

rows.text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Red muscle fibres produce ATP aerobically under normal oxygen conditions.
Mitochondria are more in white than in red muscle fibres.
Lactic acid accumulates more in red than in white muscle fibres under similar conditions.
All muscle fibres primarily produce ATP anaerobically.

rows.text: Which one of the following organisms produces the female gamete by mitosis of haploid cells?
options: Garden pea
Honey bee
Fruit fly
Chicken

rows.text: Which amino acid will be charged on the tRNA with anticodon 5'-GUU-3'?
options: Asparagine (codon AAC)
Valine (codon GUU)
Leucine (codon UUG)
Glutamine (codon CAA)

rows.text:
Two double heterozygous plants (PpQq), derived from two different pairs of true-breeding parents of unknown genotype, produce gametes in the proportions as given below.

| First cross | Second cross |
|---|---|
| ♀ R1 X ♂ R2 | ♀ R3 X ♂ R4 |
| F1 PpQq | F1 PpQq |
| 35% pQ, 35% Pq, 15% PQ, 15% pq | 35% PQ, 35% pq, 15% pQ, 15% Pq |

Which one of the following options correctly represents the genotype of the parents?
options: R1 = ppQQ ; R2 = PPqq ; R3 = PPQQ ; R4 = ppqq
R1 = PPQQ ; R2 = ppqq ; R3 = ppQQ ; R4 = PPqq
R1 = ppQQ ; R2 = PPqq ; R3 = PPqq ; R4 = ppQQ
R1 = PPQQ ; R2 = ppqq ; R3 = ppqq ; R4 = PPQQ
rows._flag: The printed cross is a two-column diagram with down arrows (parents, then F1, then gametes); typed here as a table with the column headings 'First cross' / 'Second cross' added. Nothing else changed.

options: A group of viruses with RNA genome and reverse transcriptase activity
A group of viruses with DNA genome and no reverse transcriptase activity
A group of viruses with DNA genome and reverse transcriptase activity
A group of viruses with RNA genome and no reverse transcriptase activity

rows.text:
The given picture was obtained from an agarose gel electrophoresis of a plasmid after digestion with restriction enzymes either X, Y or both X and Y.

Which one of the following diagrams correctly represents the position of the restriction enzyme sites (X, Y) on the 10,000 bp plasmid?

figure.note: Agarose gel with three lanes headed X, X + Y, Y (a well at the top of each). Lane X: one band at 5 kb. Lane X + Y: two bands, at 3 kb and 2 kb. Lane Y: one band at 5 kb. Arrows on the right mark 5 kb, 3 kb and 2 kb.

options: Circular plasmid pIAT25 with X sites at 9235 bp and 4235 bp, and Y sites at 1235 bp and 6235 bp
Circular plasmid pIAT25 with X sites at 9235 bp and 6235 bp, and Y sites at 1235 bp and 4235 bp
Circular plasmid pIAT25 with X sites at 9235 bp and 1235 bp, and Y sites at 6235 bp and 4235 bp
Circular plasmid pIAT25 with Y sites at 9235 bp and 6235 bp, and X sites at 1235 bp and 4235 bp

rows.text: Honey bee males are haploid and females are diploid. Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT about honey bees?
options: Honey bee males cannot have daughters but can have sons.
Honey bee males are produced from unfertilized eggs and females are produced from fertilized eggs.
A honey bee male does not have a father but has a grandfather.
Honey bee males form gametes by mitosis and females form gametes by meiosis.

rows.text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
options: More than 80% of the solar energy incident on earth is captured by plants and photosynthetic bacteria.
Only 10% of energy is transferred to each of the higher trophic levels in grazing food chain.
All organisms of a trophic level should be included for estimation of energy content of that trophic level.
The movement of energy is unidirectional in the ecological pyramid of energy.
